reserveReview.rationale: Removed the V2 USDB CDP and PSM groups from BUCK's direct composition and recomputed the envelope over the V1-only basis of the pinned Sui checkpoint 303739938 inventory (2026-07-27T22:52:41.565Z, recorded by the applied 2026-08-29 Codex review). Bucket's migration guide assigns the V2 CDP and PSM to the USDB liability, disables BUCK minting in phase 2, and converts BUCK to USDB 1:1 with no protocol fee; V2 collateral therefore backs USDB rather than BUCK and is recorded here as a conversion dependency instead of BUCK-owned reserve rows. The retained V1 groups are the recorded CDP bucket collateral $205,174.97, Reservoir USDC/USDT/AUSD/FDUSD/misc stable balances $69,775.39, and stable-swap LP face balances $3,074,810.29, totaling $3,349,760.65 and normalizing to 6.13%, 2.08%, and 91.79%. Verification reads taken 2026-09-05: checkpoint-pinned Reservoir object reads return $61,409.62 of direct stable balances led by USDC $59,526.08, and the V1 Well objects hold about $12,600 of further stablecoin reserves, so the recorded $69,775.39 aggregate sits between the two readings and its per-issuer split is not decomposable from the record; the group therefore stays as one aggregate row. The live census the same day shows 29 non-zero buckets against 36 at the pinned checkpoint and a Reservoir USDC balance of $54,547.71, so the legacy system remains live while it winds down. The conversion dependency is load-bearing for holders: BUCK total supply is 25,970,456.35 (BUCK TreasuryCap read 2026-09-05 and corroborated by DefiLlama), the V2 migration PSM already holds 2,218,904.46 BUCK against 2,218,904.42 USDB issued, and the BUCK savings flask holds 507,920.04 BUCK, while direct V1 collateral covers only a fraction of outstanding BUCK. BUCK held in the migration PSM, the savings flask, and the LP positions is circular or internal and excluded. This is a dated on-chain inventory, not an independent solvency attestation; stale oracle readings, heterogeneous CDP collateral, and the LP composition remain unresolved below.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Pinned Sui checkpoint 303739938 object reads from the applied 2026-08-29 Codex inventory, restricted to the V1 contracts after removing the V2 USDB CDP and PSM groups, and renormalized over the $3,349,760.65 V1-only basis; verified 2026-09-05 with checkpoint-pinned Reservoir and Well reads plus a live protocol census
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: All three rows are group-level aggregates of the dated inventory: the V1 CDP row aggregates heterogeneous on-chain collateral types (36 non-zero buckets at the pinned checkpoint) that need constituent-level valuation and dependency joins; the Reservoir stable row cannot be split by issuer from the record; and the V1 stable-swap LP positions are observed by face value with their underlying BUCK/stablecoin composition not established, so a large share of LP face may itself be circular BUCK. Several V1 token prices were stale at the pinned checkpoint, so the percentages are a dated inventory rather than a current solvency claim.

nonLinkDispositions.reserveName: BUCK V1 CDP bucket collateral (36 non-zero buckets)
nonLinkDispositions.rationale: The pinned V1 measurement observes 36 non-zero buckets, including stale-oracle and LP-like assets; no reconciled constituent table supports a safe dependency split.

The recorded $69,775.39 aggregate covers USDC, USDT, AUSD, FDUSD, and minor stables across Reservoir and related V1 objects, but the record does not decompose the per-issuer amounts, and checkpoint-pinned reads confirm the split is not recoverable without mixing measurements.

nonLinkDispositions.reserveName: BUCK V1 stable-swap LP reservoir positions
nonLinkDispositions.rationale: Cetus, Scallop, and Bluefin LP face balances are observable, but the measurement does not establish their underlying stablecoin/BUCK split or a redeemable value at the checkpoint; the BUCKETUS pool is itself a Cetus USDC/BUCK LP position, so a material share of the face value may be circular BUCK.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: Collateral is held in Bucket's on-chain CDP vaults and Peg Stability Module on Sui rather than with a legal custodian, so legal segregation, insolvency treatment, and reuse restrictions are not applicable in the traditional sense and are not separately established by the reviewed sources; wrapped-asset constituents (BTC, ETH, stablecoins) carry their own issuer and bridge custody layers.
